## Project structure

```         
X2pack/
├── .cursor/rules/      Cursor coding rules (copies of dev/rules/)
├── dev/
│   ├── plans/          Implementation plan documents
│   └── rules/          Coding rules (.mdc files)
├── doc/                This manual and other documentation
├── dist/               Production build output (git-ignored)
├── public/             Static assets (icons, favicon)
└── src/
    ├── components/     Shared UI components (UpdatePrompt)
    ├── db/             IndexedDB access layer
    ├── screens/        One file per screen + sibling .css
    ├── styles/         tokens.css, base.css
    ├── types/          index.ts — all shared TypeScript types
    ├── icon-source.svg Source artwork for all app icons
    ├── App.tsx         Screen state machine
    └── main.tsx        Entry point
```

## Quick start

### First-time setup

Run this **once** after cloning (installs npm dependencies). You can run it from the repository root, or pass the script path from anywhere:

```{bash}
bash scripts/setup-once.sh
```

If you need Python for tooling, initialise `pyenv` in your shell first (otherwise `pyenv shell ...` fails):

```{bash}
eval "$(pyenv init - zsh)"
```

### Start the dev server

```{bash}
npm run dev
```

The app is available at `http://localhost:5173`. The dev server binds to all network interfaces (`--host`), so it is also reachable from other devices on the same WiFi — see **Local iPhone testing** below.

### Local iPhone testing (development)

```{bash}
# In a separate terminal, create a tunnel to the dev server (URL of dev server must be entered here)
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:5173
# Prints an https://... URL — use that URL in Safari on your iPhone
```

> The tunnel URL changes every time you restart `cloudflared`. Install from a tunnel only for development testing — not for everyday use.

## Install on iPhone as a home-screen app

X2pack is a **Progressive Web App (PWA)**. On iPhone, Safari lets you save it to the home screen, where it opens full-screen — with its own icon, no browser chrome, and offline support.

### Requirements

- Opened in **Safari** (Chrome and Firefox on iOS cannot install PWAs)
- Served over **HTTPS**

### Steps

1. Open the app URL in **Safari** on your iPhone.
2. Tap the **Share** button (the box-with-arrow icon at the bottom of the screen).
3. Scroll the share sheet and tap **Add to Home Screen**.
4. Confirm the name ("X2pack") and tap **Add**.

The app now appears on the home screen. Tapping it opens it full-screen like a native app.

### Getting an HTTPS URL

The service worker — required for the home-screen install prompt and offline caching — only activates over HTTPS.

**For everyday use — deploy to a static host:**

Build once and push to any static hosting provider (Netlify, Vercel, etc.) — they all provide HTTPS automatically. The installed app will always open from that URL even without an internet connection (cached content). See **Deployment to a static host** below.

**For one-off testing from your Mac — HTTPS tunnel:**

Run both commands, each in its own terminal tab:

```{bash}
# Create a tunnel to the dev server (URL of dev server must be entered here)
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:5173
# Prints an https://... URL — use that URL in Safari on your iPhone
```

> The tunnel URL changes every time you restart `cloudflared`. Install from a tunnel only for development testing — not for everyday use.

## Running tests

```{bash}
# Run all unit tests once
npm test

# Watch mode (re-runs on file save)
npm run test:watch

# Generate a coverage report
npm run coverage
```

Tests live in `src/db/packLists.test.ts`. They cover the pure helper functions: `hasCircularReference`, `isDependedUpon`, and `resolveLeafLists`.

## Type checking

The build runs `tsc -b` before Vite, so a clean build implicitly type-checks. To check without building:

```{bash}
npx tsc -b --noEmit
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Production build

```{bash}
npm run build
```

Output goes to `dist/`. The folder is self-contained — upload it to any static host. The build includes:

-   Pre-bundled JS and CSS
-   `index.html`
-   `manifest.webmanifest` (PWA manifest)
-   `sw.js` + `workbox-*.js` (service worker with offline caching)

To preview the production build locally before deploying:

```{bash}
npm run preview
# Serves dist/ at http://localhost:4173
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Deployment to a static host

The `dist/` folder is the deployable artifact. Upload its contents to the web root of your hosting provider. All routes must serve `index.html` as a fallback (single-page app mode).

### Via rsync (SSH access required)

```{bash}
npm run build
rsync -avz --delete dist/ user@yourserver.com:/var/www/x2pack/
```

### Via FTP / SFTP

Use any FTP client (e.g. Cyberduck, FileZilla). Upload the contents of `dist/` to the web root. Overwrite all existing files.

### Via Netlify CLI

```{bash}
npm install -g netlify-cli
netlify deploy --prod --dir dist
```

### Via Vercel CLI

```{bash}
npm install -g vercel
vercel --prod
```

### Via GitHub Pages

GitHub Pages serves a dedicated `gh-pages` branch as a static site over HTTPS — no separate hosting account needed. Requires a public repository.

**Deploy:**

```{bash}
npm run deploy
```

This builds the app and pushes `dist/` to the `gh-pages` branch. On first run GitHub detects the branch and activates Pages automatically — no manual configuration required. The live URL follows the pattern `https://username.github.io/X2pack/` and is shown under **Settings → Pages** once active.

> **Base path:** When serving from a sub-path (i.e. no custom domain), add `base: '/X2pack/'` to `vite.config.ts` so Vite resolves assets correctly. Omit this if you point a custom domain at the site.

> **HTTPS requirement:** The service worker only activates over HTTPS. Your hosting provider must serve the site over HTTPS (virtually all modern providers do this by default via Let's Encrypt).

## PWA icons

All icon files are pre-generated and committed in `public/`. The source artwork is `src/icon-source.svg`.

| File                   | Size       | Used for                            |
|------------------------|------------|-------------------------------------|
| `pwa-192x192.png`      | 192×192 px | Android home screen                 |
| `pwa-512x512.png`      | 512×512 px | Splash screen + maskable icon       |
| `apple-touch-icon.png` | 180×180 px | iOS home screen (Add to Home Screen)|
| `favicon.svg`          | vector     | Browser tab (modern browsers)       |

To regenerate from the source SVG (requires `librsvg` — install with `brew install librsvg`):

```{bash}
rsvg-convert -w 512 -h 512 src/icon-source.svg -o public/pwa-512x512.png
rsvg-convert -w 192 -h 192 src/icon-source.svg -o public/pwa-192x192.png
rsvg-convert -w 180 -h 180 src/icon-source.svg -o public/apple-touch-icon.png
cp src/icon-source.svg public/favicon.svg
```

## Service worker and updates

The service worker is generated by `vite-plugin-pwa` (Workbox). It pre-caches all build assets on first load, enabling fully offline use thereafter.

**Update flow:**

1.  You deploy a new build to your host.
2.  When a user opens the app, the browser checks for a new service worker in the background.
3.  If a new SW is found, the `UpdatePrompt` banner appears: *"A new version is available."*
4.  The user taps **Update** — the new SW activates and the page reloads.

The app also checks for updates once per hour while it is open.

**Force-clear the service worker in development** (if caching causes stale behaviour):

Open Chrome DevTools → Application → Service Workers → click **Unregister**, then hard-reload (`Cmd+Shift+R`).

## What's New dialog

After a new version is installed, the app shows a "What's New" popover on the user's first open. It is dismissed by tapping **Got it**, the **✕** button, or anywhere on the backdrop — and will not appear again until the next version.

### How it works

`WhatsNewDialog` compares `localStorage.lastSeenVersion` against the build-time constant `__APP_VERSION__` (injected by Vite from `package.json`). When they differ, the dialog is shown. On dismiss the current version is written to `localStorage`, suppressing the dialog for that version.

```
localStorage.lastSeenVersion  ≠  __APP_VERSION__  →  show dialog
                              =  __APP_VERSION__  →  skip
```

### Setting the version number

The version is the `"version"` field in `package.json`. The build script (`npm run build`) calls `scripts/bump-version.sh` first, which prompts for a bump type and runs `npm version patch|minor|major` to update it automatically. You can also edit `package.json` directly.

Vite reads `package.json` at build time and injects the value as `__APP_VERSION__`, so the dialog always reflects exactly what is in `package.json` at the time of the build.

### Updating the changelog

**The build is gated on the changelog.** `scripts/bump-version.sh` calculates the next version number before touching `package.json`, then checks that `src/changelog.md` already contains a matching `## Version X.Y.Z` heading. If the entry is missing the script aborts without modifying `package.json`, so no phantom version is created. Only once the check passes does it write the new version and hand off to the compiler.

Edit `src/changelog.md` before building. Prepend a new top-level section for the new version:

```md
## Version X.Y.Z

### New
- **Feature name** — short description.

### Improved
- **Thing** — what changed and why it matters.
```

The file is imported at build time (`?raw`), parsed with `marked`, and rendered as HTML inside the dialog. Standard Markdown is supported: headings, bullet lists, bold/italic, horizontal rules.

### Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `src/changelog.md` | Markdown source for the dialog body |
| `src/components/WhatsNewDialog.tsx` | Component + `shouldShowWhatsNew()` helper |
| `src/components/WhatsNewDialog.css` | Styles |
| `scripts/check-changelog.sh` | Build gate — aborts if no entry for the current version |

## Data model

All data lives in IndexedDB in the browser — there is no server-side database. Two stores:

| Store       | Key         | Contents                              |
|-------------|-------------|---------------------------------------|
| `packLists` | `id` (UUID) | Predefined, reusable packing lists    |
| `packings`  | `id` (UUID) | Active and completed packing sessions |

The DB is initialised automatically on first launch. There is no migration step — the schema is defined once in `src/db/db.ts`.

**To wipe all data** (development / reset):

Open Chrome DevTools → Application → Storage → click **Clear site data**.

## Adding a new screen

1.  Create `src/screens/MyScreen.tsx` and `src/screens/MyScreen.css`.

2.  Add a new variant to the `Screen` union in `src/types/index.ts`:

   ```{ts}
    | { id: 'my-screen'; someParam: string }
    ```

3.  Import and render it in `src/App.tsx`:

    ```{tsx}
    {screen.id === 'my-screen' && (
      <MyScreen someParam={screen.someParam} onNavigate={setScreen} />
    )}
    ```

4.  Navigate to it from any other screen:

    ```{ts}
    onNavigate({ id: 'my-screen', someParam: 'value' })
    ```

See `dev/rules/navigation-architecture.mdc` for the full contract.
